question: Which specific cells in the testes are responsible for making testosterone?
explanation: Great job! The interstitial cells of Leydig are found inside the testes and do the heavy lifting of making testosterone. Keep it up! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h1)

question: What is the main job of the fluid made by the seminal vesicles?
explanation: You've got this! Seminal vesicle fluid is packed with fructose, giving sperm the energy boost they need to swim toward the egg. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h1)

question: What actually happens to the prostate gland in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)?
explanation: Spot on! 'Benign' means non-cancerous. In BPH, the prostate cells simply overgrow, which is very common as men age. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h2)

question: If an older male patient has an enlarged prostate (BPH), what urinary symptom is he most likely to complain about?

options.A: A weak and slow urinary stream

explanation: Makes total sense, right? When the prostate grows, it presses on the urethra like a pinched garden hose, making the urine flow slow and weak. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is a major sign that sets acute bacterial prostatitis apart from chronic prostate issues?

options.A: Gradual hair loss on the legs

explanation: Spot on. Acute infections hit hard and fast! Patients usually run a high fever and feel very sick, unlike chronic cases. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is it so important to figure out the exact type of prostatitis a patient has?

options.A: It indicates that immediate surgical removal of the prostate is needed
options.B: It prevents the future development of benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.C: It proves whether the patient has concurrent testicular cancer
options.D: It dictates whether antibiotics or non-infectious management is required

explanation: Brilliant! Bacterial infections need antibiotics, while other types of pelvic pain need a totally different, non-infectious treatment plan. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h3)

question: Why is testicular torsion treated as an absolute medical emergency?

options.A: It causes irreversible damage to the prostate gland
options.B: Loss of blood supply can lead to tissue death within hours
options.C: It always leads to permanent systemic high blood pressure
options.D: It immediately spreads severe infection to the kidneys

explanation: You nailed it. When the cord twists, it cuts off blood flow. If we don't fix it right away, the testicle can die. Every minute counts! [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h4)

question: During a physical exam for a patient with testicular torsion, which reflex is usually missing?
explanation: Correct! Normally, stroking the inner thigh makes the testicle rise (cremasteric reflex). In torsion, that reflex is completely absent. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h4)

question: Testicular cancer is most commonly diagnosed in which age group?
explanation: Good to know! Unlike many other cancers, testicular cancer hits younger guys, which is why teaching self-exams to this group is so vital. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h5)

question: What is the most common early sign of testicular cancer?

options.A: Sudden severe pain accompanied by a high fever
options.B: Recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood
options.C: A painless, firm lump inside the testicle
options.D: Painful swelling of the entire scrotum during walking

explanation: Spot on! Early on, it usually just feels like a painless, hard lump. That is why monthly self-checks are a lifesaver. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h5)

question: How do blood vessel (vascular) diseases lead to erectile dysfunction?

options.A: By causing excessive testosterone production in the testes
options.B: By blocking the normal production of seminal fluid
options.C: By destroying the nerves of the cremasteric muscle
options.D: By impairing adequate blood flow into the cavernous tissues

explanation: You got it! An erection needs good, healthy blood flow to fill the tissues. If vascular disease gets in the way, that flow is restricted. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the primary test used to check sperm quality when investigating male infertility?
explanation: Awesome! A semen analysis looks at how many sperm there are, how well they swim (motility), and their shape. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the best advice to give a young man on how to do a testicular self-exam?

options.A: Squeeze the epididymis firmly to check for inner fluid pockets
options.B: Perform the check monthly during or after a warm shower
options.C: Check the scrotum once a year during your annual medical exam
options.D: Examine the testicles only when experiencing lower back pain

explanation: Brilliant! Warm water relaxes the skin of the scrotum, making it much easier to feel around and notice any unusual lumps. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h7)

question: What is the most critical nursing action for a patient with a continuous bladder irrigation (CBI) catheter after prostate surgery?

options.A: Removing the indwelling catheter immediately on postoperative day one
options.B: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the drainage bag from filling
options.C: Clamping the catheter tube every hour to measure bladder capacity
options.D: Monitoring urine output color and clearing any clots to prevent blockage

explanation: You got it! CBI keeps blood clots from plugging up the catheter. As a nurse, watching the drainage color and keeping the lines clear prevents painful bladder spasms and blockages. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h7)
